name: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
challenge: Catastrophic prediction
moment: Catastrophic prediction
mechanism: Keep Event → Predict Different → Speak Plurals
goal: Ground steady attention; keep several explanations alive until new evidence separates them.
steps:
1. Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.

name: ADD THE PREFIX
title: ADD THE PREFIX
challenge: Action avoidance & procrastination
moment: Action avoidance & procrastination
mechanism: Action avoidance family: prefix thought opens a route toward resume task.
goal: Notice the thought as mental activity, then keep doing what you chose; hold deeper quiet.
steps:
1. Put “I am noticing my mind produce…” before the thought. Say the whole sentence once at normal speed.
2. Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.

name: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
challenge: Values, meaning & loss
moment: Values, meaning & loss
mechanism: Ask Danger → Answer M → Respect
goal: Keep deeper quiet: respect the warning in a thought without letting it sign the contract.
steps:
1. Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer: “I’m not signing this instruction.” Choose one action that reflects what matters to you while keeping any useful caution.
4. Respect the alarm; decline the contract.

name: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
challenge: Rigid beliefs, labels & stories
moment: Rigid beliefs, labels & stories
mechanism: Place Thought → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
goal: Watch a thought arrive and leave without helping it stay or go; keep gentle stillness.
steps:
1. Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.
2. Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one fixed visual point.
4. Another carrier may come; none owns the station.

name: NAME THE SERIES
title: NAME THE SERIES
challenge: Comparison & rejection
moment: Comparison & rejection
mechanism: Rejection magnification family: ignore opens a route toward ask whether.
goal: Enter steady pause: recognise the recurring story before treating today's episode as new evidence.
steps:
1. Ignore today’s plot for ten seconds.
2. Ask which recurring series it belongs to—‘Rejection Prediction’, ‘Everyone Is Ahead’, or ‘Fix It Now’. Give it a title and season number.
3. Then check if this episode contains new information or recycled footage.

name: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
title: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
challenge: Urges, impulses & cravings
moment: Urges, impulses & cravings
mechanism: Picture Command → Reject Authority
goal: Turn an inner command into information you can choose around; hold gentle pause.
steps:
1. Hear the command exactly as it arrives: ‘Leave now,’ ‘Check again,’ ‘You must reply.’
2. Translate it into an urge: ‘I feel an urge to leave, check, or reply.’
3. Let the urge give you information without giving it authority.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Re-enter an ordinary activity through your senses instead of demanding perfect focus — hold quiet pause.

STEPS
1. Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.

WIN
Attention wandered and returned through the next physical contact point without self-scolding.

RETURN KEY
Noise rises · ENTERACTION
Place Vision · ENTERACTION
Enter Fully · ENTERACTION

MIND BEND
Focus is not a continuous state — it is repeatedly rebuilt at the moment of return.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Ordinary → Place Vision → Leave Re → Stay Activity → Enter Fully

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not narrow attention during driving, caregiving, or tasks requiring broad awareness.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
challenge: Panic & body alarm
moment: Panic & body alarm
mechanism: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
goal: Hold steady pause: use a slow movement sequence to prove your body can follow deliberate instructions.
steps:
1. Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.

about 90 seconds

GOAL
Hold steady pause: use a slow movement sequence to prove your body can follow deliberate instructions.

name: ONE FOOT HERE, EYES OPEN
title: ONE FOOT HERE, EYES OPEN
challenge: Trauma & memory-as-present
moment: Trauma & memory-as-present
mechanism: Trauma time collapse family: press one foot opens a route toward contact support.
goal: Enter brief quiet; re-anchor in the current room without pulling more detail from the past.
steps:
1. Press one foot into the floor and keep both eyes open.
2. Look at each room corner and name one visible difference.
3. Say your current age without describing the earlier event.
4. Move farther from anything that increases the memory alarm.
5. Contact a safe person if present-time orientation stays weak.

about 1 minute

GOAL
Give pleasant, unpleasant, dull, and vivid sensations the same brief welcome; find steady anchor.

STEPS
1. Let the field choose its next foreground.

Preference itself became another event in the field instead of deciding what had to stay or leave.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Follow a sound all the way into silence without keeping it alive in memory — anchor steady focus.

STEPS
1. Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound.
2. Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
3. Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone.
4. Let the following surroundings sound end the practice.

WIN
The tone disappeared completely and the next real sound, not the remembered one, ended the practice.

RETURN KEY
Stillness thins · LISTENPAST
Follow Decay · LISTENPAST
LISTENPAST · Let Surroundings

MIND BEND
Silence is not the absence of attention. It becomes perceptible when you stop replacing a finished sound with its mental echo.

FORMULA FLOW
Play Safe → Follow Decay → Stay Silence → Let Surroundings

SAFETY
PAUSE
Avoid intense volume or tones associated with distress.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
challenge: Attention & cognitive overload
moment: Attention & cognitive overload

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Feel some inner space in the body while staying aware of the room around you; hold brief stillness.

STEPS
1. Imagine your torso and limbs as having space inside them rather than feeling like solid blocks.
2. Notice open areas and distances in that body image while still seeing and hearing the room.
3. Keep the image gentle and remember it is only an image.

WIN
Your body image felt more spacious without losing contact with the room around you.

RETURN KEY
Stillness thins · BODYINNER
Cavities · BODYINNER
BODYINNER · Keep Image

MIND BEND
The body can feel solid in your mental picture and spacious in experience. Changing the picture can shift the felt boundary.

FORMULA FLOW
Imagine Torso → Cavities → Keep Image

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop immediately if the exercise makes you feel unreal, disconnected, numb, or less oriented to the room.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

name: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
title: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
challenge: You keep fighting something that cannot be changed today

name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
challenge: Emotional reasoning
moment: Emotional reasoning
mechanism: Name Mix → Link Cue → Read Order
goal: Find quiet anchor: put blended feelings back into the order they actually arrived.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Let one thought end without immediately filling the empty beat with another; find deeper stillness.

STEPS
1. Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Allow the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count the gap only after it is over.

WIN
A real gap appeared before the next thought arrived on its own, even if it lasted only a fraction.

RETURN KEY
Quiet breaks → DONOTREPLACE
Empty → DONOTREPLACE
Count Gap → DONOTREPLACE

MIND BEND
The mind can hide silence by commenting on it. The first post-gap thought can make the gap seem absent.

FORMULA FLOW
Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap

SAFETY
PAUSE
Use external engagement if silence feels frightening or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

name: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
challenge: Rumination & worry loops
moment: Rumination & worry loops
mechanism: Name Lap → Buy Three → Close Toll
goal: Steady anchored attention: make another thinking lap pay for the time it takes from real life.
steps:
1. Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
2. Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now.
4. When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go.

name: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
challenge: Emotional reasoning
moment: Emotional reasoning
mechanism: Emotion–fact confusion family: use happened opens a route toward finish moment.
goal: Quiet rising noise: put one memory segment into past tense while inserting present facts between loaded lines.
steps:
1. Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
2. After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’

name: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
title: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
challenge: Self-blame, guilt & shame
moment: Self-blame, guilt & shame
mechanism: Make Time Zones → Reassign → Do Present Job
goal: Ground quiet pace; put past actions, present repairs, and future prevention back into their correct time zones.
steps:
1. Picture three time zones: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Place completed actions in PAST, available repair in PRESENT, and prevention plans in FUTURE.
3. Move any item that belongs to the wrong time zone.
4. Do only one PRESENT task now.

name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
challenge: Trauma & memory-as-present
moment: Trauma & memory-as-present
mechanism: Date Events → Present → Recheck Urgency
goal: Restore the real time distance between events that currently feel piled together; hold brief pause.
steps:

3. Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.

name: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
title: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
challenge: A failure feels like proof of who you are
moment: A failure feels like proof of who you are
mechanism: Emotion–fact confusion family: drop identity verb opens a route toward add condition.
goal: Quiet steady moment; turn identity verdicts into temporary processes that can change under conditions.
steps:
1. Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is.
2. Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’.
3. Add one condition under which the process changes.

moment: Action avoidance & procrastination

goal: Step back from the mind's content without stepping away from the action you own; settle steady quiet.

mechanism: Choose Object → Repeat Shift → Select Aperture
goal: Settle steady stillness; practise moving attention between tiny detail and the whole scene.

4. Move back to detail, then choose the view that best fits your task.

name: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
title: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
challenge: You are living by an old label
moment: You are living by an old label
mechanism: Action avoidance family: sort identity costs opens a route toward find the price.
goal: Measure what an identity lets you do, blocks, and demands before deciding whether it still serves you — hold steady quiet.
steps:
1. Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME.
2. Sort the identity into those three buckets.
3. Find the biggest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep.

stepsStructured.text: Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME.

PLAY TIME
45–90 seconds

GOAL
Enter brief stillness; separate what remains addressable from what is already over, then choose one proportionate next step.

STEPS
1. Name the one piece of the event you are still carrying.
2. Separate what can still be addressed from what is already over.
3. Choose one reasonable next step, or deliberately choose to leave the event finished.

WIN
The carried part of the event became either a reasonable action or a deliberate decision to leave it finished.

RETURN KEY
CLEARASKIGNITION · Anchor slips
CLEARASKIGNITION · Ask Clearly
CLEARASKIGNITION · Close Loop

Resentment keeps the past active when it cannot tell whether there is still a job to do. Separating repairable from over creates an exit.

Use Detail → Ask Clearly → Close Loop

name: DOORWAY FIRST
title: DOORWAY FIRST

moment: Getting defensive before they finish in the moment
mechanism: Verbal naming + micro-action interrupts premature defence by moving the doorway toward the actual message.

5. Use the shortest honest sentence that still tells the truth.

name: MOTIVATION OR FRICTION?
title: MOTIVATION OR FRICTION?
challenge: A team member seems disengaged
moment: A team member seems disengaged
mechanism: Observation–hypothesis separation + one diagnostic question interrupts motivation guessing by testing friction before judging intent.
goal: Find out whether disengagement is really low motivation or a fixable blocker before judging the person — find steady stillness.
steps:

3. Pick one question that could separate low motivation from a practical blocker.
4. Ask it neutrally, or prepare to ask: “What is making this hard to move?”
5. Set one small next step from what you learn.

name: WHO YOU CHOOSE NEXT
title: WHO YOU CHOOSE NEXT
challenge: You fear the thought says something about who you are
moment: You fear the thought says something about who you are
mechanism: Defusion + values choice separate an involuntary intrusive thought from identity by letting chosen behaviour, not mental content, supply the next piece of evidence.
goal: Hold deeper stillness; keep a disturbing thought separate from identity and let the next chosen action represent you instead.
steps:
1. Catch the thought and leave it uninterpreted.
2. Say, “My mind produced this; it is not my biography.”
3. Name one priority you want to stand for in the next minute—kind, honest, patient, careful, brave, or another word that fits.
4. Do one ten-second action aligned with that principle.
5. Leave the thought unanswered and continue with the action.
